# Azure Resource Manager Cosmos client library for Java

Azure Resource Manager Cosmos client library for Java

For documentation on how to use this package, please see [Azure Management Libraries for Java](https://aka.ms/azsdk/java/mgmt).

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- [Java Development Kit (JDK)][jdk] with version 8 or above
- [Azure Subscription][azure_subscription]

### Adding the package to your product

[//]: # ({x-version-update-start;com.azure.resourcemanager:azure-resourcemanager-cosmos;current})
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.azure.resourcemanager</groupId>
    <artifactId>azure-resourcemanager-cosmos</artifactId>
    <version>2.56.0-beta.1</version>
</dependency>
```
[//]: # ({x-version-update-end})

### Include the recommended packages

Azure Management Libraries require a `TokenCredential` implementation for authentication and an `HttpClient` implementation for HTTP client.

[Azure Identity][azure_identity] package and [Azure Core Netty HTTP][azure_core_http_netty] package provide the default implementation.

### Authentication

Microsoft Entra ID token authentication relies on the [credential class][azure_identity_credentials] from [Azure Identity][azure_identity] package.

Azure subscription ID can be configured via `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
Azure tenant ID can be configured via `AZURE_TENANT_ID` environment variable.

Assuming the use of the `DefaultAzureCredential` credential class, the client can be authenticated using the following code:

```java readme-sample-authenticate
AzureProfile profile = new AzureProfile(AzureEnvironment.AZURE);
TokenCredential credential = new DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder()
    .authorityHost(profile.getEnvironment().getActiveDirectoryEndpoint())
    .build();
CosmosManager manager = CosmosManager
    .authenticate(credential, profile);
```

The sample code assumes global Azure. Please change `AzureEnvironment.AZURE` variable if otherwise.

See [Authentication][authenticate] for more options.

## Key concepts

See [API design][design] for general introduction on design and key concepts on Azure Management Libraries.

## Examples

decisions.reason: The authenticate overloads and Configurable adapter construct a manager and pipeline (CosmosManager lines 29-77), but the complete class has no @Generated comparison or customization-script operation; the supplied material does not establish that these facade factories were handwritten rather than emitted by the management SDK generator.

The constructor supplies a profile-selected endpoint, pipeline and subscription to the builder (CosmosManager lines 79-85). That is concrete cloud-aware construction, but the file's unknown source kind and lack of an annotated-neighbor or script edit leave generator ownership unresolved.

The databaseAccounts getter lazily caches a collection facade (CosmosManager lines 92-97); neither this behavior nor the absence of annotations proves it is handwritten. No generated baseline or customization-script edit for this manager is supplied.

The account constructor calls fixDBName and the helper lowercases with Locale.ROOT (account implementation lines 62-67 and 549-551), but the fluent implementation has unknown generation provenance. A nontrivial transform in an implementation class is not by itself a handwritten signal.

The getter joins IP rule strings and the setter splits comma-separated input into models (account implementation lines 89-95 and 385-395). The transformation is real, but no generation comparison or customization edit shows these facade methods are handwritten.

ipRules returns an unmodifiable view, not a defensive copy (account implementation lines 97-100). The supplied unknown-kind fluent implementation does not distinguish an intentionally handwritten collection view from a generated helper.

defaultConsistencyLevel throws on a missing policy and otherwise projects its level (account implementation lines 107-114). The guard is present, but no evidence identifies this member as handwritten or as a change from generated output.

The bound and collection listKeys methods map generated results to a wrapper whose accessors forward four key properties (account lines 126-138, collection lines 120-138, wrapper lines 10-34). A typed wrapper and synchronous bridge can also be generated management implementation helpers; no handwritten provenance is shown.

listReadOnlyKeys maps to a two-property forwarding wrapper with blocking synchronous counterparts (account lines 140-152, collection lines 125-148, wrapper lines 10-24). The complete captured wrapper contains no signal distinguishing handwritten adaptation from generator-emitted implementation.

The connection-string result is wrapped and its accessor returns the inner list (account lines 154-166, collection lines 150-164, wrapper lines 12-21).
